animals/bee: "stays inside its nest with others through cold winters": true of honeybees (the ordinary sense); bumblebee colonies die off and only the queens overwinter, alone
"works with others in its colony to gather and store supplies": honeybees store nectar and pollen; solitary bees do not live in colonies
animals/deer: "bounds away with its white tail raised when startled": characteristic of white-tailed deer; other species (roe, red deer) flash a pale rump patch rather than raising a white tail
"has a reddish-brown summer coat that turns greyer in winter": true of white-tailed, roe and red deer; not all species
animals/dolphin: "has a long snout filled with many small pointed teeth": true of most dolphins (bottlenose, common); a few (e.g. Risso's) have short snouts and few teeth
animals/fox: "is sometimes killed by eagles, lynx and coyotes": documented for red foxes (golden eagles, Eurasian lynx, coyotes in North America); a lay reader may not know it
animals/frog: "can spend winter dormant in the mud of pond bottoms": true of some kinds (e.g. leopard and green frogs, which mostly rest on the bottom rather than burrow deep); others overwinter on land
animals/mouse: "eats seeds and grains, sometimes storing them in its nest": food caching is well known in field and deer mice; house mice cache less
animals/rabbit: "gives birth to blind, hairless young in a sheltered nest": true of the European rabbit and cottontails; hares, a close relative, bear furred, open-eyed young
animals/snake: "sheds its outer layer of skin several times as it grows": frequency varies by age and species, but several sheds a year is typical
animals/wolf: "has yellow or amber eyes that stand out against its fur": typical of adult wolves; eye colour varies somewhat
